units.zh: 柴守禮
units.en: Chai Shouli
units.literal: Chai Shouli

units.zh: 周太祖聖穆皇后柴氏，無子，養後兄守禮之子以為子，是為世宗。
units.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan, wife of Later Zhou's Taizu, bore no sons. She adopted her elder brother Shouli's son as her own; that child became Shizong.
units.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai, of Zhou Taizu had no son; she adopted the son of her elder brother Shouli as her own, and this was Shizong.

units.zh: 守禮字克讓，以後族拜銀青光祿大夫、檢校吏部尚書、兼御史大夫。
units.en: Shouli, courtesy name Kerang, was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Personnel, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief on account of his ties to the empress's clan.
units.literal: Shouli, style name Kerang, by virtue of the empress's kin was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Personnel, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 世宗即位，加金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空、光祿卿。
units.en: When Shizong ascended the throne he was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Minister of Works, and Director of the Imperial Household.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne he was further given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Minister of Works, and Director of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 致仕，居於洛陽，終世宗之世，未嘗至京師，而左右亦莫敢言，第以元舅禮之，而守禮亦頗恣橫，嘗殺人於市，有司有聞，世宗不問。
units.en: He retired to Luoyang and never once came to the capital during Shizong's entire reign, yet no one at court dared raise the matter; they could only honor him as the emperor's maternal uncle. Shouli was also quite overbearing and once killed a man in the marketplace. When officials reported it, Shizong took no action.
units.literal: He retired and lived in Luoyang. Throughout Shizong's reign he never came to the capital, yet those around the throne dared not speak of it; they merely treated him with the rites due an imperial maternal uncle. Shouli was also rather overbearing and once killed a man in the marketplace. When the authorities reported it, Shizong made no inquiry.

units.zh: 是時，王溥、汪晏、王彥超、韓令坤等同時將相，皆有父在洛陽，與守禮朝夕往來，惟意所為，洛陽人多畏避之，號「十阿父。」
units.en: At the time Wang Pu, Wang Yan, Wang Yanchao, Han Lingkun, and others were serving together as generals and chief ministers. Each had a father living in Luoyang who kept company with Shouli day and night and did as they pleased. The people of Luoyang mostly feared and avoided them, calling them the "Ten Foster Fathers."
units.literal: At that time Wang Pu, Wang Yan, Wang Yanchao, Han Lingkun, and others were simultaneously generals and chief ministers; each had a father in Luoyang who associated with Shouli morning and evening, doing as they pleased. Many in Luoyang feared and avoided them, calling them the "Ten Foster Fathers."

units.zh: 守禮卒年七十二，官至太傅。
units.en: Shouli died at seventy-two, having risen to Grand Tutor.
units.literal: Shouli died at seventy-two, having reached the office of Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 嗚呼，父子之恩至矣！
units.en: Alas—the bond between father and son is the deepest of all!
units.literal: Alas, the bond between father and son reaches its utmost!

units.zh: 孟子言：舜為天子，而瞽叟殺人，則棄天下，竊負之而逃。
units.en: Mencius said that if Shun were emperor and his father Gusou killed a man, Shun would abandon the realm, secretly carry his father on his back, and flee.
units.literal: Mencius said: If Shun were Son of Heaven and his father Gusou killed a man, he would abandon the realm, secretly carry his father on his back, and flee.

units.zh: 以謂天下可無舜，不可無至公，舜可棄天下，不可刑其父，此為世立言之說也。
units.en: The point is that the realm might do without Shun but not without supreme justice; Shun might abandon the throne but not punish his father. That is the teaching offered for the world.
units.literal: The meaning is that the realm can do without Shun but cannot do without supreme impartiality; Shun can abandon the realm but cannot punish his father—this is doctrine set forth for the world.

units.zh: 然事固有不得如其意者多矣！
units.en: Yet in real affairs things often cannot go as one wishes!
units.literal: Yet in affairs there are indeed many cases where one cannot have things as one wishes!

units.zh: 蓋天子有宗廟社稷之重、百官之衛、朝廷之嚴，其不幸有不得竊而逃，則如之何而可？
units.en: The Son of Heaven bears the ancestral temple, the altars of state, the guard of all officials, and the dignity of court. If misfortune prevents him from slipping away in secret, what then can he do?
units.literal: For the Son of Heaven bears the weight of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, the guard of the hundred officials, and the majesty of court—if by misfortune he cannot steal away and flee, what then is to be done?

units.zh: 予讀周史，見守禮殺人，世宗寢而不問，蓋進任天下重矣，而子於其父亦至矣，故寧受屈法之過，以申父子之道，其所以合於義者，蓋知權也。
units.en: Reading the history of Zhou, I see that when Shouli killed a man Shizong let the matter drop. He put the weight of the realm first, yet a son's duty to his father also stood at its height. He would rather bear the fault of bending the law than violate the bond between father and son. That this was righteous shows he knew how to weigh circumstances.
units.literal: When I read the history of Zhou and saw that Shouli killed a man yet Shizong suppressed the matter and did not inquire, I understood that he advanced the weight of the realm while a son's duty to his father also reached its utmost. Thus he would rather accept the fault of bending the law to fulfill the way of father and son. That this accorded with righteousness lay in knowing how to weigh circumstances.

units.zh: 君子之於事，擇其輕重而處之耳。
units.en: In all affairs the noble person simply weighs what matters more and what matters less, then acts accordingly.
units.literal: The noble man in affairs simply chooses what is lighter and heavier and acts accordingly.

units.zh: 失刑輕，不孝重也。
units.en: To fail in administering punishment is a light matter; to be unfilial is a heavy one.
units.literal: Failure in punishment is light; unfilial conduct is heavy.

units.zh: 刑者所以禁人為非，孝者所以教人為善，其意一也，孰為重？
units.en: Punishment restrains people from wrong; filial piety teaches them to do good. Their purpose is the same. Which weighs more?
units.literal: Punishment is what restrains people from wrongdoing; filial piety is what teaches people to do good—their purpose is one. Which is heavier?

units.zh: 刑一人，未必能使天下無殺人，而殺其父，滅天性而絕人道，孰為重？
units.en: Punishing one man may not stop killing in the realm, but to execute one's own father is to extinguish one's nature and sever the human bond. Which weighs more?
units.literal: To punish one man may not necessarily keep the realm free of killing, but to kill one's father extinguishes one's inborn nature and cuts off the human way—which is heavier?

units.zh: 權其所謂輕重者，則天下雖不可棄，而父亦不可刑也。
units.en: Weigh what is light against what is heavy, and even if the realm cannot be abandoned, a father still cannot be punished.
units.literal: Weigh what is called light and heavy, and though the realm cannot be abandoned, a father also cannot be punished.

units.zh: 然則為舜與世宗者，宜如何無使瞽叟、守禮至於殺人，則可謂孝矣！
units.en: For men like Shun and Shizong, true filial piety would mean keeping Gusou and Shouli from ever killing in the first place.
units.literal: Then for one such as Shun or Shizong, how ought one act so that Gusou and Shouli never come to killing—only then may one be called filial!

units.zh: 然而有不得如其意，則擇其輕重而處之焉。
units.en: When things cannot go as one wishes, one must still choose the lighter and heavier course and act on that basis.
units.literal: Yet when one cannot have things as one wishes, one chooses the light and heavy and acts accordingly.

units.zh: 世宗之知權，明矣夫！
units.en: How clear it is that Shizong knew how to weigh circumstances!
units.literal: Shizong's knowledge of weighing circumstances—how clear it is!

units.zh: 世宗三皇后。
units.en: Shizong had three empresses.
units.literal: Shizong had three empresses.

units.zh: 貞惠皇后劉氏，不知其世家，蓋微時所娶也，世宗為左監門衞將軍，得封彭城縣君。
units.en: Empress Zhenhui of the Liu clan—her family background is unknown; she was probably wed in his humble early days. While Shizong served as general of the Left Gate Guard, she received the title Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.
units.literal: Empress Zhenhui, née Liu—her lineage is unknown; she was likely married in humble times. When Shizong was general of the Left Gate Guard, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.

units.zh: 世宗從太祖于魏，后留京師，太祖舉兵，漢誅其族。
units.en: Shizong followed Taizu to Wei while the empress stayed behind in the capital. When Taizu took up arms, Later Han put his entire clan to death.
units.literal: Shizong followed Taizu to Wei; the empress remained in the capital. When Taizu raised troops, Later Han executed his clan.

units.zh: 太祖即位，追封彭城郡夫人。
units.en: After Taizu ascended the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.

units.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月，始詔彭城郡夫人劉氏追冊為皇后，有司謚曰貞惠，陵曰惠陵。
units.en: In the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, an edict at last posthumously installed Lady Liu of Pengcheng as empress. The responsible offices gave her the posthumous title Zhenhui, and her mausoleum was named Huiling.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, an edict finally posthumously installed Lady Liu of Pengcheng Commandery as empress; the responsible offices gave the posthumous title Zhenhui, and her mausoleum was called Huiling.

units.zh: 宣懿皇后符氏
units.en: Empress Xuanyi of the Fu clan
units.literal: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu

units.zh: 宣懿皇后符氏，其祖秦王存審，父魏王彥卿。
units.en: Empress Xuanyi of the Fu clan was descended from Prince of Qin Cunshen on her grandfather's side and from Prince of Wei Yanqing on her father's.
units.literal: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu—her grandfather was Prince of Qin Cunshen; her father, Prince of Wei Yanqing.

units.zh: 後世王家，出於將相之貴，為人明果有大志。
units.en: She came from a later generation of that princely house, born to the nobility of generals and ministers. Clever, resolute, and ambitious, she was a woman of uncommon force of character.
units.literal: The lady came from a later generation of the princely house, born of the nobility of generals and ministers; as a person she was clear-minded, resolute, and possessed of great ambition.

units.zh: 初適李守貞子崇訓。
units.en: She was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.
units.literal: At first she was married to Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun.

units.zh: 守貞事漢為河中節度使，已挾異志。
units.en: Shouzhen served Later Han as military governor of Hezhong and already nursed rebellious ambitions.
units.literal: Shouzhen served Han as military governor of Hezhong and already harbored rebellious intent.

units.zh: 有術者善聽人聲以知吉兇，守貞出其家人使聽之，術者聞後聲，驚曰：「此天下之母也！」
units.en: A diviner skilled at reading fortune from the human voice examined Shouzhen's household. When he heard the lady speak he cried out in alarm: "This is the mother of the realm!"
units.literal: There was a practitioner skilled at listening to human voices to know fortune and misfortune. Shouzhen brought out his household for him to hear; when the practitioner heard the lady's voice he exclaimed in alarm, "This is the mother of the realm!"

units.zh: 守貞益自負，曰：「吾婦猶為天下母，吾取天下復何疑哉！」
units.en: Shouzhen grew still more confident. "If even my wife is to be mother of the realm," he said, "what doubt can I have about seizing the empire!"
units.literal: Shouzhen grew all the more self-assured and said, "Even my wife is to be mother of the realm—what doubt have I about taking the realm!"

units.zh: 於是決反。
units.en: With that he resolved on rebellion.
units.literal: Thereupon he resolved to rebel.

units.zh: 而漢遣周太祖討之，逾年，攻破其城。
units.en: Later Han sent Later Zhou's Taizu against him. More than a year later the city fell.
units.literal: Han sent Taizu of Zhou to punish him; after more than a year the city was taken.

units.zh: 崇訓知不免，手自殺其家人，次以及後，後走匿，以帷幔自蔽，崇訓惶遽求後不得，遂自殺。
units.en: Knowing escape was impossible, Chongxun killed his family with his own hand, then turned on his wife. She fled and hid behind hanging curtains. Frantic, he could not find her and killed himself.
units.literal: Chongxun knew he could not escape and with his own hand killed his household members, next intending the lady. She fled and hid, screening herself with curtains. Chongxun searched for her in panic without finding her, then killed himself.

units.zh: 漢兵入其家，後儼然坐堂上，顧軍士曰：「郭公與吾王父有舊，汝輩無犯我！」
units.en: When Han soldiers entered the house she sat composed in the hall and told the troops: "Lord Guo and my grandfather were old friends—you must not touch me!"
units.literal: When Han troops entered the house the lady sat composed in the hall, turned to the soldiers, and said, "Lord Guo and my grandfather were old friends—you must not harm me!"

units.zh: 軍士見之不敢迫。
units.en: Seeing her bearing, the soldiers did not dare approach.
units.literal: The soldiers, seeing her, did not dare press close.

units.zh: 太祖聞之，以謂一女子能使亂兵不敢犯，奇之，為加慰勉，以歸彥卿。
units.en: Taizu marveled that one woman could hold disorderly troops at bay. He comforted her and sent her back to Yanqing.
units.literal: When Taizu heard of it he thought it marvelous that a single woman could keep disorderly troops from violating her; he comforted and encouraged her and returned her to Yanqing.

units.zh: 後感太祖不殺，拜太祖為父。
units.en: Grateful that Taizu had spared her life, she acknowledged him as her adoptive father.
units.literal: Grateful that Taizu had not killed her, the lady acknowledged Taizu as her father.

units.zh: 其母以後夫家滅亡，而獨脫死兵刃之間，以為天幸，欲使削髮為尼，後不肯曰：「死生有命，天也。
units.en: Her mother, seeing that her son-in-law's house had been destroyed while she alone escaped the swords, took it for heaven's mercy and wanted her to take the tonsure. The lady refused: "Life and death are heaven's decree.
units.literal: Her mother, because the lady's husband's house had been destroyed yet she alone escaped death amid blades, thought it heaven's fortune and wished her to shave her head and become a nun. The lady refused, saying, "Life and death are ordained by heaven.

units.zh: 何必妄毀形發為！」
units.en: Why should I rashly destroy my body and shave my hair!"
units.literal: Why vainly destroy one's form and hair!"

units.zh: 太祖於後有恩，而世宗性特英銳，聞後如此，益奇之。
units.en: Taizu had shown her kindness, and Shizong, whose nature was keen and bold, admired her all the more when he heard how she had acted.
units.literal: Taizu had shown the lady kindness, and Shizong's nature was especially keen and sharp; hearing how she had acted, he admired her all the more.

units.zh: 及劉夫人卒，遂納以為繼室。
units.en: After Lady Liu died he took her as his next wife.
units.literal: When Lady Liu died he took the lady as his successor wife.

units.zh: 世宗即位，冊為皇后。
units.en: When Shizong became emperor he installed her as empress.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne he installed her as empress.

units.zh: 世宗辦急多暴怒，而後嘗追悔，每怒左右，後必從容伺顏色，漸為解說，世宗意亦隨解，由是益重之。
units.en: Shizong was quick-tempered and prone to violent anger, yet he often regretted it afterward. Whenever he raged at those around him the empress would calmly watch his mood and gently reason with him until his anger passed. He valued her all the more for this.
units.literal: Shizong was impatient and often flew into rage, yet afterward he would regret it. Whenever he grew angry with those around him the empress would calmly watch his expression and gradually explain and persuade; Shizong's mood would ease with hers, and for this he valued her all the more.

units.zh: 世宗征淮，後以帝不宜親行，切諫止之，世宗不聽。
units.en: When Shizong campaigned against Huai she urged earnestly that the emperor should not take the field in person. He would not listen.
units.literal: When Shizong campaigned against Huai the empress urged that the emperor ought not go in person and admonished him earnestly to stop; Shizong would not listen.

units.zh: 師久無功，遭大暑雨，後以憂成疾而崩。
units.en: The campaign dragged on without success through fierce summer rains. The empress fell ill from worry and died.
units.literal: The army was long without success and met great heat and rain; the empress fell ill from worry and died.

units.zh: 議者以方用兵，請殺喪禮，於是百官朝臨於西宮，三日而釋服，帝亦七日而釋，葬於新鄭，陵曰懿陵。
units.en: Because the army was still campaigning, counselors asked that mourning be shortened. Officials attended at the Western Palace for three days and then left mourning dress; the emperor did the same after seven days. She was buried at Xinzheng in Yiling Mausoleum.
units.literal: Counselors, because troops were still in the field, requested curtailed mourning rites. Thereupon the hundred officials attended morning audience at the Western Palace; after three days they left mourning dress, and the emperor also after seven days. She was buried at Xinzheng; the mausoleum was called Yiling.

units.zh: 後立皇后符氏，
units.en: Later, another Lady Fu was established as empress,
units.literal: Later, another Lady Fu was established as empress,

units.zh: 后妹也。
units.en: The new empress was her younger sister.
units.literal: she was the former empress's younger sister.

units.zh: 國初，遷西宮，號周太后。
units.en: At the dynasty's founding she was moved to the Western Palace and styled Dowager of Zhou.
units.literal: At the founding of the dynasty she was moved to the Western Palace and styled Dowager of Zhou.

units.zh: 世宗子七人：長曰宜哥，次二皆未名，次曰恭皇帝，次曰熙讓，次曰熙謹，次曰熙誨，皆不知其母為誰氏。
units.en: Shizong had seven sons: the eldest was called Yige; the next two were never named; then came Emperor Gong, followed by Xirang, Xijin, and Xihui. The identity of each mother is unknown.
units.literal: Shizong had seven sons: the eldest was called Yige; the next two were never named; next came Emperor Gong; then Xirang, Xijin, and Xihui—the mothers of all of them are unknown.

units.zh: 宜哥與其二，皆為漢誅。
units.en: Yige and the next two were all put to death by Later Han.
units.literal: Yige and the second two were all executed by Later Han.

units.zh: 太祖即位，詔賜皇孫名誼，贈左驍衞大將軍；
units.en: When Taizu took the throne, an edict bestowed names on the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard;
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict bestowed names on the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously granted Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard;

units.zh: 誠，左武衞大將軍；
units.en: Cheng, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard;
units.literal: Cheng, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard;

units.zh: 諴，左屯衞大將軍。
units.en: and Kan, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard.
units.literal: Kan, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard.

units.zh: 顯德三年，群臣請封宗室，世宗以謂為國日淺，恩信未及於人，而須功德大成，慶流於世，而後議之可也。
units.en: In Xiande 3 the ministers asked to enfeoff the imperial clan. Shizong replied that the state was still young, that favor and trust had not yet reached the people, and that enfeoffment should wait until merit was complete and blessings flowed to the realm.
units.literal: In the third year of Xiande the ministers requested enfeoffment of the imperial clan. Shizong held that the state had been founded only recently, favor and trust had not yet reached the people, and one must wait until merit and virtue were fully achieved and blessings flowed through the age—only then might the matter be discussed.

units.zh: 明年夏四月癸未，先封太祖諸子。
units.en: On guiwei day in the fourth month of the following summer he first enfeoffed Taizu's sons.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the following year, on the day guiwei, he first enfeoffed Taizu's sons.

units.zh: 又詔曰：「父子之道，聖賢不忘，再思天閼之端，愈動悲傷之抱。
units.en: He also decreed: "The way between father and son is never forgotten by the sages. Thinking again how heaven first closed its gate upon us, my grief grows only deeper.
units.literal: He also issued an edict: "The way of father and son—the sages and worthies do not forget it. Thinking again of the beginning of heaven's bereavement, my bosom of grief is stirred all the more.

units.zh: 故皇子左驍衛大將軍誼、左武衛大將軍諴、左屯衛大將軍誠等，載惟往事，有足傷懷，宜增一字之封，仍贈三臺之秩。
units.en: My late sons, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Kan, and Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard Cheng, recall past sorrows that still wound the heart. Let their titles be raised by one degree and let them receive the ranks of the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: The late imperial sons, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Kan, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard Cheng, and others—reflecting on past events, there is much to wound the heart. They should receive an added character in their enfeoffment and still be granted the ranks of the Three Dais.

units.zh: 誼可贈太尉，追封越王；
units.en: Yi shall be posthumously made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Yue;
units.literal: Yi may be posthumously granted Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Yue;

units.zh: 誠太傅，吳王；
units.en: Cheng shall be Grand Tutor and Prince of Wu;
units.literal: Cheng, Grand Tutor, Prince of Wu;

units.zh: 諴太保，韓王。」
units.en: Kan shall be Grand Guardian and Prince of Han."
units.literal: Kan, Grand Guardian, Prince of Han."

units.zh: 而皇子在者皆不封。
units.en: The imperial sons who were still alive received no enfeoffment.
units.literal: Yet the imperial sons still living were none of them enfeoffed.

units.zh: 六年，北復三關，遇疾，還京師。
units.en: In the sixth year he recovered the Three Passes in the north, fell ill, and returned to the capital.
units.literal: In the sixth year, he recovered the Three Passes in the north, fell ill, and returned to the capital.

units.zh: 六月癸未，皇子宗訓，特進左衞上將軍，封梁王；
units.en: On guiwei day in the sixth month, the imperial son Zongxun was specially advanced to Grand General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;
units.literal: On guiwei day in the sixth month, the imperial son Zongxun was specially advanced to Grand General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;

units.zh: 而宗讓亦拜左驍衞上將軍，封燕國公。
units.en: Zongrang was also appointed Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
units.literal: Zongrang was also appointed Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

units.zh: 後十日而世宗崩，梁王即位，是為恭皇帝。
units.en: Ten days later Shizong died. The Prince of Liang ascended the throne—this was Emperor Gong.
units.literal: Ten days later Shizong died; the Prince of Liang took the throne—this was Emperor Gong.

units.zh: 其年八月，宗讓更名熙讓，封曹王。
units.en: In the eighth month of that year, Zongrang was renamed Xirang and enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.
units.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Zongrang was renamed Xirang and enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.

units.zh: 熙謹、熙誨皆前未封爵，遂拜熙謹右武衞大將軍，封紀王；
units.en: Xijin and Xihui had not previously received titles; Xijin was then appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;
units.literal: Xijin and Xihui had previously received no enfeoffment; Xijin was then appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;

units.zh: 熙誨左領軍衞大將軍，蘄王。
units.en: and Xihui was made Grand General of the Left Army Guard and Prince of Qi.
units.literal: Xihui was made Grand General of the Left Army Guard and Prince of Qi.

units.zh: 皇朝乾德二年十月，熙謹卒。
units.en: In the tenth month of Qiande 2 under the Song, Xijin died.
units.literal: In the tenth month of Qiande 2 of the Imperial Dynasty, Xijin died.

units.zh: 熙讓、熙誨，不知其所終。
units.en: The final fates of Xirang and Xihui are unknown.
units.literal: As for Xirang and Xihui, their ends are unknown.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 至公，天下之所共也。
units.en: Supreme justice is what the whole realm holds in common.
units.literal: Supreme impartiality is what the realm shares in common.

units.zh: 其是非曲直之際，雖父愛其子，亦或有所不得私焉。
units.en: At the turning point between right and wrong, even a father who loves his son may not always show favoritism.
units.literal: At the juncture of right and wrong, crooked and straight, even a father who loves his son may sometimes be unable to show partiality.

units.zh: 當周太祖舉兵於魏，漢遣劉銖誅其家族於京師，酷毒備至；
units.en: When Later Zhou's Taizu raised his army in Wei, Later Han sent Liu Zhu to slaughter his entire household in the capital with every cruelty imaginable;
units.literal: When Taizu of Zhou raised troops in Wei, Han sent Liu Zhu to exterminate his clan in the capital, cruelty reaching its utmost;

units.zh: 後太祖入立，遣人責銖，銖辭不屈，太祖雖深恨之，然以銖辭直，終不及其家也。
units.en: after Taizu took the throne he sent men to reproach Zhu. Zhu answered without yielding. Taizu hated him deeply, yet because Zhu's words were upright he never harmed his family.
units.literal: later, when Taizu entered and took the throne, he sent men to reproach Zhu. Zhu's words did not yield; though Taizu deeply hated him, because Zhu's words were upright he ultimately did not touch his household.

units.zh: 及追封妻子之被殺者，其言深自隱痛之而已，不敢有非漢之辭焉，蓋知其曲在己也。
units.en: When he posthumously honored the wife and children who had been killed, his language expressed only private grief; he dared not speak ill of Later Han, for he knew the fault lay with himself.
units.literal: When he posthumously enfeoffed the wife and sons who had been killed, his words were only deep self-concealed grief; he dared not speak against Han—for he knew the wrong lay with himself.

units.zh: 故略存其辭，以見周之有愧於其心者矣！
units.en: I preserve his words here in brief to show that Later Zhou carried a burden of conscience in its heart!
units.literal: Therefore I briefly preserve his words, to show that Zhou had cause for shame in his heart!

units.zh: 既而諸大臣以恩之所被，皆朝廷親近之臣，而宗室劉信及青州劉銖等皆國家元勛，必有不平之意，且外慮諸侯以朝廷有私於親近也，於是議及四方侯伯，普加恩焉。
units.en: Then the great ministers reflected that those favored were all the court's intimate ministers, while the imperial clansman Liu Xin, Qing Prefecture's Liu Zhu, and others were all founding merit of the state and would surely feel discontent. They also feared that feudal lords would think the court showed partiality to intimates. Therefore they discussed extending favor to the lords and princes throughout the realm.
units.literal: Then the great ministers reflected that those on whom favor had fallen were all the court's intimate ministers, while the imperial clansman Liu Xin and Qing Prefecture's Liu Zhu and others were all founding merit of the state and would surely feel discontent—and moreover they feared externally that feudal lords would think the court showed partiality to intimates—so they discussed extending favor to the lords and princes of the four directions universally.

units.zh: 己未，許州劉信加兼侍中，開封尹侯益進封魯國公，鄆州慕容彥超、青州劉銖並加兼侍中。
units.en: On jiwei, Liu Xin of Xu Prefecture was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu, and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou and Liu Zhu of Qing Prefecture were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
units.literal: On jiwei, Xu Prefecture Liu Xin was given the additional title of Palace Attendant; Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu; Yunzhou Murong Yanchao and Qing Prefecture Liu Zhu were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 皇弟熙誨拜金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、左領衛大將軍，封蘄王，食邑三千戶。
units.en: The emperor's younger brother Xihui was appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and acting Minister of Education, made great general of the Left Leading Guards and Prince of Qi with three thousand fief households.
units.literal: The imperial younger brother Xihui was appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Minister of Education, and Great General of the Left Leading Guards, enfeoffed as Prince of Qi with a fief income of three thousand households.

units.zh: 及明崔甗之謗言，執侯景之奸使，昔人稱孟軻為勇，于文簡公見之。
units.en: When he exposed Cui Yan's slander and seized Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, one can see in Duke Wenjian the courage that earlier men praised in Meng Ke.
units.literal: When he exposed Cui Yan's slanderous words and seized Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, what men of old called Meng Ke's courage can be seen in Duke Wenjian.

units.zh: 癸未，立魏王符彥卿女為皇后，仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。
units.en: On guiwei, the daughter of Fu Yanqing, Prince of Wei, was installed as empress, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day for the investiture ceremony.
units.literal: On guiwei, the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was installed as empress; the responsible offices were further ordered to choose a day and prepare the rites of investiture.

units.zh: 以皇長子宗訓為特進左衛上將軍，封梁王；
units.en: The eldest son Zongxun was made specially advanced general of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;
units.literal: The eldest imperial son Zongxun was made specially advanced General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;

units.zh: 甲午，宣遺制，梁王於柩前即皇帝位，服紀月日一依舊制。
units.en: On jiawu, the testamentary edict was proclaimed; the Prince of Liang took the throne before the bier, with mourning observances following the established calendar.
units.literal: On jiawu, the testamentary edict was proclaimed; the Prince of Liang assumed the imperial throne before the bier, and the mourning calendar of months and days followed the old regulations.

units.zh: 以第二子宗讓為左驍衛上將軍，封燕國公。
units.en: the second son Zongrang was made general of the Left Tiger Swift Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
units.literal: the second son Zongrang was made General of the Left Tiger Swift Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

units.zh: 是日，群臣奉梁王即位於殿東楹，中外發哀。
units.en: That day the officials installed the Prince of Liang at the hall's eastern pillar, and mourning was proclaimed throughout the realm.
units.literal: That day the officials installed the Prince of Liang at the eastern pillar of the hall; court and country raised mourning.

units.zh: 放勛、重華之世，咸無意於受終，當塗、典午之君，雖有心於揖讓，皆以英才處萬乘，高勳御四海，故能大庇黔首，光宅區縣。
units.en: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.
units.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.

units.zh: 既而煙雲表色，日月呈瑞，緯聚東井，龍見譙邦，除舊布新，既彰玄象，遷虞事夏，且協謳訟，[2]九域八荒，同布衷款，百神群祀，皆有誠願。
units.en: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.
units.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.

units.zh: 梁氏以天祿斯改，期運永終，欽若唐、虞，推其鼎玉，朕東西退讓，拜手陳辭，避舜子於箕山之陽，求支伯於滄洲之野，而公卿敦逼，率土翹惶，天命難稽，遂享嘉祚。
units.en: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne.
units.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.

units.zh: 八月甲戌朔，以光祿卿致仕柴守禮為太子太保致仕。
units.en: On the first day jiaxu of the eighth month, Chai Shouli, retired Director of the Imperial Household, was made retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day jiaxu, Chai Shouli, retired Director of the Imperial Household, was made retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：符後先適河中節度使李守貞之子崇訓。
units.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu Hou had first married Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun.
units.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu Hou had first been married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen, the military governor of Hezhong.

units.zh: 及城陷，後獨免，周祖為世宗娶之，顯德中，冊為後。）〉
units.en: When the city fell she alone was spared. The Zhou founder had her marry his heir Shizong, and in the Xiande era she was made empress.)〉
units.literal: When the city fell, Hou alone was spared. The Zhou founder had her marry Shizong, and in the Xiande era she was enfeoffed as empress.)〉

units.zh: 〈（《琬琰集》載《宋實錄·王全斌傳》云：同光末，蕭牆有變，亂兵逼宮城，近臣宿將，皆釋甲潛遁，惟全斌與符彥卿等十數人居中拒戰。
units.en: (The 《Collected Writings》 cites the 《Song Veritable Records · Wang Quanbin Biography》: at the end of Tongguang, palace mutiny drove rebels against the capital; close ministers and veteran generals shed armor and fled; only Quanbin, Fu Yanqing, and a dozen others held the center to fight.
units.literal: (The 《Collected Writings》 records the 《Song Veritable Records · Wang Quanbin Biography》 as saying: at the end of Tongguang, turmoil rose within the palace walls; rebel troops pressed the palace city; close ministers and veteran generals all doffed armor and fled in secret; only Quanbin and Fu Yanqing and more than ten others held the center to resist.

units.zh: 《東都事略·符彥卿傳》云：郭從謙之亂，莊宗左右皆引去，惟彥卿力戰，殺十餘人。
units.en: The 《Outline of the Eastern Capital · Fu Yanqing Biography》 says that in Guo Congqian's revolt Zhuangzong's attendants all fled; only Yanqing fought hard and killed more than ten men.
units.literal: The 《Outline of the Eastern Capital · Fu Yanqing Biography》 says: at Guo Congqian's rebellion Zhuangzong's attendants all withdrew; only Yanqing fought fiercely and killed more than ten.

units.zh: 莊宗崩，彥卿慟哭而去。）〉
units.en: When Zhuangzong died, Yanqing wept and left.)〉
units.literal: When Zhuangzong died Yanqing wept and left.)〉

units.zh: 是月，周主威殂，養子晉王柴榮嗣立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Guo Wei died, and his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded him.
units.literal: That month Zhou ruler Wei died; his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 是月，周主榮殂，子宗訓立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.
units.literal: That month, Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使李守貞為前軍都虞候。
units.en: Palace Guards cavalry commander Li Shouzhen was made vanguard chief adjutant.
units.literal: Li Shouzhen, commander of the Palace Guards horse army, was made chief adjutant of the vanguard.

units.zh: 開運元年春正月甲戌朔，是夕陣雲掩北斗之魁星。
units.en: On the first day jiaxu of the first month of spring in Kaiyun 1, battle clouds that night veiled the leader star of the Northern Dipper.
units.literal: In spring, the first month, first day jiaxu of the first year of Kaiyun, that night battle clouds covered the leader star of the Northern Dipper.

units.zh: 丁亥，敵騎至黎陽。
units.en: On dinghai enemy cavalry reached Liyang.
units.literal: On dinghai, enemy horsemen reached Liyang.

units.zh: 太祖即位，詔賜皇孫名，誼贈左驍衛大將軍，誠左武衛大將軍，諴左屯衛大將軍。
units.en: When Taizu acceded he named his grandsons: Yi became Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Cheng of the Left Martial Guard, and Yan of the Left Garrison.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict granted names to the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Cheng Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and Yan Grand General of the Left Garrison.

units.zh: 故皇子左驍衛大將軍誼、左武衛大將軍誠、左屯衛大將軍諴等，載惟往事，有足傷懷，宜增一字之封，仍贈三臺之秩。
units.en: My sons Yi, Cheng, and Yan—honored as generals of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Martial Guard, and Garrison—deserve remembrance that still pains me. Let each receive a fuller princely title and a post in the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: The late princes, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Cheng, and Grand General of the Left Garrison Yan and others—reflecting on past events, there is ample cause for wounded feeling; they should receive an added character in their enfeoffment and still be granted ranks among the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 誠太傅，吳王；
units.en: Cheng Grand Tutor and Prince of Wu;
units.literal: Cheng as Grand Tutor, Prince of Wu;

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·家人傳》云：世宗子七人，長曰宜哥，次二皆未名，次曰恭皇帝，次曰熙讓，次曰熙謹，次曰熙誨，皆不知其母為誰氏，宜哥與其二皆為漢誅。
units.en: Ouyang Xiu's family biographies record seven sons of Shizong: the eldest Yige, two younger boys still unnamed, then the future Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui. Their mothers are unknown. Yige and the two unnamed boys were killed by the Later Han.
units.literal: The "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History says: Shizong had seven sons; the eldest was called Yige, the next two were both unnamed, the next was the Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui; it is not known who their mothers were; Yige and the other two were all executed by the Han.

units.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州龍崗人，世家豪右。
units.en: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, born into the Chai clan of Longgang in Xingzhou, came from a family that had long ranked among the region's great houses.
units.literal: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, née Chai, was a native of Longgang in Xingzhou; her family were for generations eminent local magnates.

units.zh: 故夫人柴氏，代籍貽芳，湘靈集慶。
units.en: Lady Chai of old, her clan's fragrance handed down through generations, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.
units.literal: Thus Lady Chai, her clan's fragrance handed down, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.

units.zh: 既而有司上謚曰聖穆。
units.en: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.
units.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.

units.zh: 宜正號於軒宮，俾潛耀於坤象，可追命為皇后。
units.en: Let her receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly realm; she is posthumously invested as Empress.
units.literal: She should receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly trigram; she may be posthumously invested as Empress.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張永德傳》云：周太祖柴後，本唐莊宗之嬪御也。
units.en: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Zhang Yongde, states that Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.
units.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Zhang Yongde》: the Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.

units.zh: 太祖微時，在洛陽聞後賢淑，遂聘之。
units.en: While he was still obscure, he heard in Luoyang of her virtue and refinement and took her as his wife.
units.literal: When the Emperor was still obscure, in Luoyang he heard that the lady was virtuous and refined, and thereupon took her in marriage.

units.zh: 莊宗沒，明宗遣歸其家，行至河上，父母迓之，會大風雨，止於逆旅數日。
units.en: After Zhuangzong's death Mingzong sent her home; on the way to the Yellow River her parents came out to meet her, but a violent storm forced them to halt at an inn for several days.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong died, Mingzong sent her back to her family; on the road she reached the river, her parents came to meet her, and they were stopped by a great storm at an inn for several days.

units.zh: 世宗皇帝即後之侄也，幼而謹願，後甚憐之，故太祖養之為己子。
units.en: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful even as a boy, he won her deep affection, and the Emperor therefore raised him as his own son.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful and prudent from youth, she pitied him deeply, so the Emperor raised him as his own son.

units.zh: 太祖即位，乃下制曰：「義之深無先於作配，禮之重莫大於追崇。
units.en: After he took the throne he issued an edict: "In depth of righteousness nothing precedes the bond of marriage; in weight of ritual nothing surpasses posthumous honor.
units.literal: When the Emperor took the throne he issued an edict saying, "In depth of righteousness nothing comes before taking a spouse; in weight of ritual nothing is greater than posthumous elevation.

units.zh: 太祖嘗寢，後見五色小蛇入顴鼻間，心異之，知其必貴，敬奉愈厚，未及貴而厭代。
units.en: Once while he slept she saw a small five-colored serpent slip between his cheek and nose; struck by the omen and sure he was destined for greatness, she honored him all the more—yet she died before he rose to power.
units.literal: Once when the Emperor was asleep, the lady saw a small serpent of five colors enter between his cheek and nose; her heart marveled at it, knowing he would surely become exalted, and she served him with ever greater respect, yet before he attained eminence she died.

units.zh: 顯德初，太祖神主入廟，以後祔於其室。
units.en: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, she was enshrined beside him in his chamber.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, the lady was enshrined with him in his chamber.

units.zh: 後見之，驚曰：「此何人邪？」
units.en: The lady saw him and cried out in surprise, "Who is this?"
units.literal: The lady saw him and said in astonishment, "Who is this man?"

units.zh: 後曰：「此貴人也，不可失也。
units.en: She replied, "This man is destined for greatness; we must not let him slip away.
units.literal: The lady said, "This man is of noble rank; he must not be let go.

units.zh: 囊中裝分半與父母，我取其半。」
units.en: She split her purse in two, gave half to her parents, and kept the rest."
units.literal: She divided the contents of her purse in half for her parents and kept half for herself."

units.zh: 父母知不可奪，遂成婚於逆旅中。
units.en: Seeing they could not dissuade her, her parents consented and the wedding was held at the inn.
units.literal: Her parents knew they could not prevail, and the marriage was completed at the inn.

units.zh: 後異其人，欲嫁之，請於父母。
units.en: Struck by his bearing, she wished to marry him and pleaded with her parents.
units.literal: The lady thought him extraordinary and wished to marry him; she asked her parents.

units.zh: 太祖壯年，喜飲博，好任俠，不拘細行，後規其太過，每有內助之力焉。
units.en: In his prime he drank and gambled freely, loved bold adventure, and cared little for petty propriety; she checked his excesses and was a steady force within the household.
units.literal: In his prime the Emperor loved drinking and gambling, delighted in chivalric adventure, and did not trouble over small proprieties; the lady admonished him when he went too far and often gave him strength within the household.

units.zh: 太祖佐漢之初，屬聖穆皇后棄世，聞妃之賢，遂以禮聘之。
units.en: Early in his service to the Later Han, after Empress Shenmu's death, he heard of the lady's virtue and took her as his wife with full ceremony.
units.literal: At the beginning when the Emperor aided Han, as Empress Shenmu had passed away, hearing of the lady's virtue he took her in marriage with full rites.

units.zh: 太祖自聖穆皇后蚤世以來屢失邦媛，中幃內助惟妃存焉，加以結珮脫簪，率由令範。
units.en: Since Empress Shenmu's early death he had lost consort after consort; she alone remained to manage the inner household, and in every detail of dress and deportment she set the standard.
units.literal: Since Empress Shenmu's early death the Emperor had repeatedly lost consorts of the state; within the inner curtain she alone remained as household help, and moreover in tying sashes and removing hairpins she always followed the fine model.

units.zh: 故昭義節度使李嗣昭、故幽州節度使周德威、故汴州節度使符存審，並配饗莊宗廟廷。
units.en: Li Sizhao, Zhou Dewei, and Fu Cunshen were given collateral offerings in Zhuangzong's temple.
units.literal: The late Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao, late Youzhou military commissioner Zhou Dewei, late Bianzhou military commissioner Fu Cunshen—all were collaterally offered in Zhuangzong's temple hall.

units.zh: 句望生蟜牛。蟜牛生瞽叟。
units.en: Gouwang fathered Jiaoniu. Jiaoniu fathered Gusou.
units.literal: Gouwang begot Jiaoniu. Jiaoniu begot Gusou.

units.zh: 瞽叟生重華，是為帝舜。
units.en: Gusou fathered Chonghua, who was Emperor Shun.
units.literal: Gusou begot Chonghua; this was Emperor Shun.

units.zh: 以蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威為權樞密使、檢校司徒；
units.en: Guo Wei was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;
units.literal: Guo Wei, chief clerk of tribal and Han forces, was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;

units.zh: 壬辰，翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼撰進貞惠皇后廟歌辭。
units.en: On renchen Dou Yan, Hanlin academician and overseer of ceremonies, presented the temple hymn for Empress Zhenhui.
units.literal: On renchen, Dou Yan, Hanlin Academician and overseer of the Directorate of Ceremonies, drafted and presented the temple hymn text for Empress Zhenhui.

units.zh: 十一月壬寅朔，葬世宗皇帝於慶陵，以貞惠皇后劉氏祔焉。
units.en: On the first day renyin of the eleventh month Emperor Shizong was buried at Qingling, with Empress Zhenhui, Lady Liu, interred beside him.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day renyin, Emperor Shizong was buried at Qingling, with Empress Zhenhui, Lady Liu, joined in burial.

units.zh: 徐州行營都部署王彥超馳奏，收復徐州。
units.en: Wang Yanchao, Commander-in-Chief of the Xuzhou field headquarters, urgently reported the recapture of Xuzhou.
units.literal: Wang Yanchao, Commander-in-Chief of the Xuzhou Field Headquarters, sent an urgent memorial reporting the recovery of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·韓令坤傳》云：倫法當棄市，令坤泣請於世宗，遂免死。）〉
units.en: (The Song History, Biography of Han Lingkun, records that Lun deserved public execution; Lingkun wept and begged Shizong, and his life was spared.)〉
units.literal: (The Song History, Biography of Han Lingkun, says: Lun by law deserved execution in the marketplace; Lingkun wept and begged Shizong, and he was spared death.)〉

units.zh: 倫，侍衛馬軍都指揮使令坤之父也。
units.en: Lun was the father of Ling Kun, commander of the palace cavalry.
units.literal: Lun was the father of Ling Kun, commander of the Palace Cavalry.

units.zh: 令坤領陳州，倫在州干預郡政，掊斂之暴，公私患之，為項城民武都等所訟。
units.en: While Ling Kun held Chenzhou, Lun meddled in local government and extorted so brutally that both officials and commoners suffered; the people of Xiangcheng, led by Wu Du, brought suit against him.
units.literal: Ling Kun held Chenzhou; Lun in the prefecture interfered in county government and extorted with violence, troubling public and private alike, and was sued by Wu Du of Xiangcheng and others.

units.zh: 以翰林學士、中書舍人王溥為戶部侍郎充職，以左司郎中、充樞密直學士景範為左諫議大夫充職。
units.en: Wang Pu (Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter) was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue; Jing Fan (Left Department director and military affairs direct academician) was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor.
units.literal: Wang Pu, Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter, was made Vice Minister of Revenue to fill the post; Jing Fan, Left Department director and concurrently direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Left Remonstrance Counselor to fill the post.

units.zh: 故皇孫三人：宜哥贈左驍衛大將軍，賜名誼；
units.en: Three late imperial grandsons: Yige received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Swift Horse Guard and the name Yi;
units.literal: Three late imperial grandsons: Yige was posthumously made General of the Left Swift Horse Guard and given the name Yi;

units.zh: 庚子，故吳國夫人張氏追贈貴妃；
units.en: On gengzi day, the late Lady Zhang of Wu was posthumously created Noble Consort;
units.literal: On the day gengzi, the late Lady Zhang, Lady of the State of Wu, was posthumously honored as Noble Consort;

units.zh: 故皇子贈左屯衛大將軍諴再贈太保，追封韓王。
units.en: and the late Prince Xian, posthumously a grand general of the Left Garrison Guard, was further honored as Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
units.literal: the late prince Xian, posthumously made Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard, was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

units.zh: 熙謹拜光祿大夫、檢校太保、右武衛大將軍，封紀王，食邑三千戶；
units.en: Xijin was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Grand Guardian, made great general of the Right Martial Guards and Prince of Ji with three thousand fief households;
units.literal: Xijin was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Guardian, and Great General of the Right Martial Guards, enfeoffed as Prince of Ji with a fief income of three thousand households;

units.zh: 宣懿皇后符氏，祖存審，事後唐武皇、莊宗，位極將相，追封秦王。
units.en: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu, was granddaughter of Cunshen, who served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong, rose to the highest ranks of general and minister, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
units.literal: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu; her grandfather Cunshen served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong, rose to the summit of general and minister, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 既而有司上謚曰宣懿，葬於新鄭，陵曰懿陵。
units.en: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Xuanyi; she was buried at Xinzheng in the tomb named Yiling.
units.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Xuanyi; she was buried at Xinzheng, tomb named Yiling.

units.zh: 後性和惠，善候世宗之旨，世宗或暴怒於下，後必從容救解，世宗甚重之，及即位，冊為皇后。
units.en: Gentle and kind by nature, she read Shizong's moods well; when he flew into rages at his subordinates she would calmly intercede on their behalf. He valued her deeply, and when he took the throne he invested her as Empress.
units.literal: The lady's nature was gentle and kind; she was skilled at reading Shizong's intent; when Shizong sometimes raged at subordinates, the lady always calmly interceded and rescued them; Shizong greatly valued her, and when he took the throne she was invested as Empress.

units.zh: 史臣曰：周室后妃凡六人，而追冊者四，故中闈內則，罕得而聞，惟董妃、符後之懿範，亦無愧於彤管矣。
units.en: The historiographer remarks: The Zhou house had six consorts in all, four of them posthumously invested; little is therefore known of the inner palace and its rules—yet the exemplary conduct of Lady Dong and Empress Fu would not disgrace the red brush.
units.literal: The historiographer says: The consorts of the Zhou house numbered six in all, of whom four were posthumously invested; hence the inner quarters and household rules are rarely heard of—only the fine models of Lady Dong and Empress Fu are without shame before the red brush.

units.zh: 父彥卿，天雄軍節度使，封魏王。
units.en: Her father Yanqing was military governor of the Tianxiong army and held the title Prince of Wei.
units.literal: Her father Yanqing was military governor of the Tianxiong army and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 後初適李守貞之子崇訓。
units.en: She was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.
units.literal: The lady was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.

units.zh: 世宗鎮澶淵日，太祖為世宗聘之。
units.en: When Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan, the Emperor betrothed her to him.
units.literal: On the day when Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan, the Emperor betrothed her to Shizong.

units.zh: 太祖入河中，令人訪而得之，即遣女使送於其父，自是後常感太祖大惠，拜太祖為養父。
units.en: When the Emperor entered Hezhong he had her found and at once sent a female envoy to return her to her father. From then on she was deeply grateful for his kindness and acknowledged him as her adoptive father.
units.literal: When the Emperor entered Hezhong he had men seek and obtain her, and at once sent a female envoy to deliver her to her father; from then on the lady always felt the Emperor's great kindness and acknowledged him as adoptive father.

units.zh: 〈（案：世宗有後符後，即宣懿之女弟也，薛史不為立傳，未免闕略。
units.en: (Note: Shizong later had another consort, Lady Fu, the younger sister of Empress Xuanyi; Xue's History gives her no separate biography, which is a regrettable omission.
units.literal: (Note: Shizong had a later consort, the later Lady Fu, who was the younger sister of Xuanyi; Xue's History did not compose a separate biography for her, which is somewhat an omission.

units.zh: 漢乾祐中，守貞叛於河中，太祖以兵攻之，及城陷，崇訓自刃其弟妹，次將及後，後時匿於屏處，以帷箔自蔽，崇訓倉黃求後不及，遂自刎，後因獲免。
units.en: During the Han Qianyou era Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and the Emperor besieged him. When the city fell, Chongxun killed his younger siblings and was about to kill her next; she had hidden behind a screen, shielded by curtains. He searched for her in panic but could not find her in time and cut his own throat, and she escaped.
units.literal: In Qianyou of Han, Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; the Emperor attacked with troops, and when the city fell Chongxun himself slew his younger siblings; next he was about to reach the lady, but she was then hiding behind a screen, covering herself with curtains; Chongxun in haste sought the lady but could not reach her and thereupon cut his own throat—the lady thereby escaped harm.

units.zh: 顯德二年七月二十一日，崩於滋德殿，時年二十有六。
units.en: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of Xiande 2 she died in Zide Hall at the age of twenty-six.
units.literal: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of the second year of Xiande she died in Zide Hall—she was twenty-six.

units.zh: 世宗將南征，後常諫止之，言甚切直，世宗亦為之動容，洎車駕駐於淮甸，久冒炎暑，後因憂恚成疾。
units.en: When Shizong prepared to campaign south she often urged him to stay, speaking with blunt earnestness that moved him; but when the imperial train halted in the Huai region, long exposure to summer heat and anxiety brought on her illness.
units.literal: When Shizong was about to campaign south, the lady often admonished and stopped him, her words very earnest and direct; Shizong was also moved by this; when the imperial carriage halted in the Huai region, long exposed to summer heat, the lady fell ill from worry and distress.

units.zh: 至世宗即位，納為皇后。
units.en: When Shizong took the throne he made her his Empress.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne she was taken in as Empress.
